concepts.title: Functions of bounded variation
concepts.blurb:
$u\in\mathrm{BV}(\Omega)$ iff $u\in L^1$ and the distributional derivative $Du$ is a finite vector-valued Radon measure on $\Omega$, with total variation $|Du|(\Omega)=\sup\{\int u\,\mathrm{div}\,\phi:\phi\in C^1_c,|\phi|\le 1\}$. Every BV function admits a Lebesgue-Radon-Nikodym decomposition $Du=
abla u\,\mathcal{L}^n + (u^+ - u^-)
u_u\,\mathcal{H}^{n-1}estriction J_u + D^c u$ — absolutely continuous, jump, and Cantor parts, supported on $\mathcal{L}^n$, on the rectifiable jump set $J_u$, and on a Cantor-like set respectively. BV is strictly larger than $W^{1,1}$ (the Heaviside has $u'=\delta_0
otin L^1$; the Cantor staircase has $
abla u\equiv 0$ but $|D^c u|=1$), enjoys $L^1$-lower-semicontinuity of $|Du|$ and Rellich-type compactness, and is the operative class for §2's perimeter theory and §6's Mumford-Shah segmentation — the natural domain whenever the admissible functions must accommodate jumps along $(n{-}1)$-rectifiable singular sets.

concepts.title: Sets of finite perimeter and reduced boundary
concepts.blurb: $E\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ has finite perimeter iff $\chi_E\in\mathrm{BV}_{\mathrm{loc}}$, with perimeter $P(E)=|D\chi_E|(\mathbb{R}^n)$ — the divergence-test sup that agrees with $\mathcal{H}^{n-1}(\partial E)$ on smooth $E$. The reduced boundary $\partial^*E$ is the set of points where the measure-theoretic outward normal $\nu_E(x)=-\lim_r D\chi_E(B_r(x))/|D\chi_E|(B_r(x))$ exists in $S^{n-1}$; corners drop out as $\mathcal{H}^{n-1}$-null. De Giorgi's structure theorem: $\partial^*E$ is countably $(n-1)$-rectifiable, $D\chi_E=-\nu_E\,\mathcal{H}^{n-1}\restriction\partial^*E$, and $P(E)=\mathcal{H}^{n-1}(\partial^*E)$. This generalizes surface area to corner-y and disconnected sets while excluding wild boundaries (Koch snowflake has $P=\infty$, ruled out); the natural domain for the isoperimetric inequality $P(E)\ge n\omega_n^{1/n}|E|^{(n-1)/n}$ and downstream existence for Plateau in §5.

concepts.title: Rectifiable sets and Hausdorff measure
concepts.blurb: $S\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is countably $k$-rectifiable iff $\mathcal{H}^k$-almost all of $S$ is contained in a countable union of Lipschitz images of $\mathbb{R}^k$ — Rademacher's theorem then supplies $\mathcal{H}^k$-a.e. tangent planes. Three equivalent characterizations classify the class: existence of approximate $k$-tangent planes $\mathcal{H}^k$-a.e.; the $k$-density $\Theta^k(S,x)=\lim_r\mathcal{H}^k(S\cap B_r)/\omega_k r^k$ equals $1$ a.e.; and the Besicovitch-Federer projection theorem — for purely $k$-unrectifiable sets, projection onto $\mathcal{H}^{k(n-k)}$-a.e. $k$-plane has Lebesgue measure zero. The 4-corner Cantor set ($\dim_H=1$ but purely $1$-unrectifiable) is the canonical counterexample; De Giorgi's $\partial^*E$ is the canonical example, and rectifiability of level sets ($\S 4$) is what makes the coarea formula well-posed.

concepts.title: Area and coarea formulas
concepts.blurb: For Lipschitz $f:\mathbb{R}^k\to\mathbb{R}^n$ ($k\le n$), the area formula $\int_A J_f\,d\mathcal{L}^k = \int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\mathcal{H}^0(A\cap f^{-1}(y))\,d\mathcal{H}^k(y)$ generalizes change-of-variables to non-injective Lipschitz maps via the multiplicity factor; injective $f$ recovers $\mathcal{H}^k(f(A))=\int_A J_f$. Both formulas hold under Lipschitz regularity (not $C^1$) thanks to Rademacher. For $u:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m$, the coarea formula $\int g\,J_u\,d\mathcal{L}^n = \int_{\mathbb{R}^m}\int_{u^{-1}(y)} g\,d\mathcal{H}^{n-m}\,d\mathcal{L}^m(y)$ slices a top-dimensional integral via level sets — most-cited as $\int|\nabla u|=\int\mathcal{H}^{n-1}(\{u=t\})\,dt$, the bridge between BV total variation and integrated level-set perimeter. Operationally this means minimizing $\int|\nabla u|$ reduces to simultaneously minimizing perimeters of superlevel sets — what makes BV the right setting for free-boundary variational problems.

concepts.title: Currents and Federer–Fleming compactness
concepts.blurb: A $k$-current $T\in\mathcal{D}^k(\mathbb{R}^n)$ is a continuous linear functional on smooth compactly-supported $k$-forms; oriented submanifolds $M$ give integration currents $\langle [M],\omega\rangle=\int_M\omega$. The boundary $\partial T$ satisfies $\langle\partial T,\eta\rangle=\langle T,d\eta\rangle$ — Stokes built into the definition, so $\partial[M]=[\partial M]$. The mass $\mathbf{M}(T)=\sup_{|\omega|\le 1}\langle T,\omega\rangle$ generalizes $\mathcal{H}^k$, and integral currents are the rectifiable, integer-multiplicity subclass closed under weak limits with bounded mass+boundary-mass. Federer-Fleming compactness: a sequence $T_j\subset\mathbf{I}_k$ with $\mathrm{spt}(T_j)\subset K$ (a fixed compact set) and uniformly bounded $\mathbf{M}(T_j)+\mathbf{M}(\partial T_j)$ admits a weakly convergent subsequence in the integral-current class; without spt-compactness mass can escape to infinity. This is the existence engine for Plateau-style problems and SBV-based segmentation in §6.

concepts.title: Applications: Plateau, minimal surfaces, and Mumford–Shah
concepts.blurb: GMT solves Plateau's problem rigorously: minimize mass over integral currents with prescribed boundary; Federer-Fleming gives existence and Allard's regularity theorem gives interior $C^{1,\alpha}$-smoothness $\mathcal{H}^k$-a.e. on the support of a stationary integral varifold (with the Simons cone in $\mathbb{R}^8$ exhibiting the first singular minimizer in codimension 1). Mumford-Shah image segmentation $\inf\int(u-g)^2 + \alpha\int_{\Omega\setminus K}|\nabla u|^2 + \beta\,\mathcal{H}^{n-1}(K)$ is well-posed via the SBV compactness theorem (Ambrosio 1989), with De Giorgi-Carriero-Leaci density estimates closing the singular set $K$. Brakke flows generalize mean-curvature flow to varifolds whose mass decreases at squared mean curvature, and Cheeger constants $h(\Omega)=\inf P(E)/|E|$ control the Laplacian spectral gap via $\lambda_1\ge h^2/4$ — both natively expressed in the perimeter / SBV / varifold language built up over the previous five sections.
